name: Mount Harvard
generated_description:
Mount Harvard rises to 14,421 feet in Colorado. With roughly 2,359 feet of topographic prominence, it stands well above the surrounding terrain. The Mount Harvard Trail covers 2.2 miles with about 1,227 feet of elevation gain — a steady climb. It's rated Moderate overall.

The Route

The grade is back-loaded: the first half of the route climbs gently, and most of the elevation gain comes in the second half. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 0.92, gaining roughly 2,300 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 13,996 feet, the route tops out near 14,278 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 38.904, -106.29749 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 80 miles west of Colorado Springs, Colorado. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

The reliable snow-free window is roughly July through September. At this elevation, afternoon thunderstorms are a serious summer hazard — start early and plan to be off the upper mountain by midday. Outside that window expect snow travel and bring traction and navigation skills to match.

Know Before You Go

The Moderate rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 1.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Mount Belford, Mount Yale and La Plata Peak — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 38.904, -106.29749 in Colorado. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.answer: July through September is the reliable snow-free window. Start early to avoid afternoon thunderstorms above treeline.

faqs.question: How tall is Mount Harvard?
faqs.answer: Mount Harvard stands at 14,421 feet (4,396 meters) in Colorado.
